conclusion: Four simple weather-tool calls returned expected structured arguments and one solid-red image was identified correctly. OpenCode 1.19.5 located and read a local fixture and returned its secret word, but repeated 4K-context compaction continued after the answer; the experiment was manually stopped. A handful of requests cannot establish stability, real coding performance, safety, or VRAM peaks.

conclusion: The WebSocket sidecar streamed partial French transcripts and exactly recovered one locally synthesized test phrase while replaying it at real-time speed. This does not establish microphone behavior, accuracy over a representative corpus, or end-to-end voice latency.
next: Connect a real microphone and compare STT candidates against a consented corpus.

command: Windows GPU Adapter Memory and GPU Process Memory performance counters during EXP-006
conclusion: A single late snapshot showed substantial model-process shared GPU memory and high system-RAM use. The model was stopped. After stopping it, adapter dedicated use was 5792108544 bytes and shared use 159502336 bytes. SSD paging caused by this process was not measured; these are not peak statistics.
next: Use smaller quantized models and collect baseline-versus-load peak VRAM, shared GPU memory, system RAM and global page-file measurements.

command: Both llama-server instances: GGML_VK_DISABLE_COOPMAT=1, -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0; node scripts/test-gateway-delegation.mjs
conclusion: Two quantized models coexisted and an OpenCode read-only task completed while the voice controller answered a follow-up and streamed speech. An earlier attempt duplicated the task and produced a confused reply; after preserving coherent turn history and deduplicating identical active tasks, the repeated probe completed with one task. RAM fell near 6 GiB available; sampled global page-file usage was about 3.8 GiB, with no pre-load baseline for causal attribution. Short sampled peaks and tiny tasks are insufficient to validate sustained 24 GB operation, live audio or agent capability.
next: Measure clean baseline, both GPU process allocations, page-file deltas, long contexts, live microphone interruption and real coding; test SYCL XMX and alternatives.

conclusion: The official SYCL build detected the B60 and produced valid tool calls with Q8 KV and Flash Attention. The first request was extremely slow; later requests were under one second with prompt-cache reuse. Different backend builds and a tiny sample prevent a fair speed ranking. Shared GPU allocations are not automatically proof of weight eviction.
next: Repeat with identical builds, cold/warm and longer prompts, controlled memory baselines, and XMX kernel verification.

command: User compared live microphone interaction with typed input while the microphone was stopped; node scripts/probe-tts-jitter.mjs
conclusion: User reported chopped or incomplete assistant speech with the microphone active, but complete speech from typed input with microphone stopped. This supports microphone feedback or false interruption as a working hypothesis, not a proven cause. A speaker-safe mode was added that gates microphone input during playback and requires manual interruption; automatic spoken barge-in in this mode is not implemented.
next: Have the user retest speaker-safe mode, then measure echo and genuine spoken interruptions with consent and compare headphones.

conclusion: Clean synthetic speech was recognized; shifted same-speaker overlap added or corrupted words and white noise produced unrelated text. One synthetic phrase is not a representative corpus; no WER, live latency or real speaker-separation result is established.
next: Evaluate consented French recordings and a licensed causal target-speaker extraction checkpoint under the concurrent resource budget.
